summary: The team is locked out of email due to stale passwords, while marketing priorities are set on Asia Star and Intelligent China, and the Knowledge website redesign is moving forward with a refined layout.
summaryDetail: The immediate fire is the Outlook account lockout affecting the whole team—everyone must delete and re-login to email accounts on all devices and contact CKGSB IT to confirm the backend unlock. On the marketing front, the team has decided to prioritize the Asia Star and Intelligent China programs, with Berkeley as a potential third; Joseph needs to draft target areas and the team must analyze participant profiles and audit conversion tracking to support this. The Knowledge website redesign is progressing: the team favored keeping the current layout with menu categorization improvements, inspired by Joseph's editorial style; Joseph will share the HTML design file and the team will hold a 30-minute feedback session and review inner pages. Upcoming: Ira will share the ESG report draft with Julie next week, and the team must prepare for the Nov 13 EuroCham Shanghai event by aligning on outstanding items and speaker lineup.

decisions.text: Stale saved passwords on devices caused repeated failed logins and account lockout; all devices must be updated.
Keep the current Knowledge layout rather than a dramatic revamp, with menu categorization as the main change.
Remove the standalone videos section and disperse videos by topic instead.
Use Joseph's design as inspiration for displaying more articles and surfacing indices, not as a final template.
Do not add a stock-market ticker at the top of the homepage.
Bring the BCI banner (and BSI) into the Knowledge section.
Prioritize Asia Star and Intelligent China programs for marketing, with Berkeley as a potential third priority.
